concerns.text: T002 requires unit tests exercising stiction and non-clamped cases and outputs conforming to estimator_output.schema.yaml, but the schema declares `epsilon_clamped` and `is_valid` with `const: true`. Any test emitting `epsilon_clamped: false` (the normal, non-stiction case) fails schema validation, making T002's verification self-contradictory and unexecutable as written. The schema must allow boolean false for these fields.

T007 instructs 'if predicted power < 0.8, re-run T005 with --num_objects up to 20', but FR-003 mandates 'exactly 10' novel objects. The task directs the implementer to violate the spec with no amendment; an implementer cannot deterministically decide whether to follow FR-003 or T007. Either amend FR-003 or make the escalation conditional on a recorded spec amendment.

Neither T004 nor T005 specifies HOW the adaptive policy consumes the estimator during episodes. FR-001 requires k_norm computed 'at every simulation timestep' and the AdaptiveRewardScheduler must adjust rewards mid-episode, but T004 only says the environment 'logs per-timestep' signals to CSV. The implementer needs an explicit statement that the estimator is invoked online inside the episode loop (not post-hoc from CSV, as plan.md T015b implies), otherwise the adaptive policy is functionally identical to static.

T009 verifies the ≤ 7 GB peak-memory budget (SC-004) 'via tracemalloc', which only tracks Python-heap allocations and will not see PyBullet/torch C-level memory. The named verification cannot produce valid evidence for SC-004; specify process RSS (e.g., resource.getrusage or psutil) instead.

T010's verification requires 'the ≥ 15% improvement check for SC-001 and ≥ 10% for SC-002', but SC-001/SC-002 in the spec are [deferred] with no pinned thresholds. The task's pass/fail check is unexecutable against a deferred criterion — either the SCs must be resolved or T010 must state which reference (acceptance scenarios vs. SCs) governs the conclusion flag.

Tasks write sweep rows to data/results/sweep.csv, but the sweep schema's description names data/generated/sweep.csv. T009's contract test and T012's documentation will disagree about the artifact path; pick one path and align schema description and tasks.

T004 is too coarse: it bundles the PyBullet environment, the novel-object generator, and the end-to-end smoke pipeline in one task. Flag for atomization into at least three tasks (env, generator, smoke run) so each has a single verifiable deliverable.

T006 says 'normalizing by / partial-correlating against N' — two different analyses joined by a slash. Name the one to implement (partial correlation controlling for N is the stronger choice) so the verification is deterministic.
